div.head: Wl Lond 3
div.ab: ⁊ ic ƿylle, þæt ælc cyld beo his fæder yrfnume æfter his fæder dæge.
Et uolo, quod omnis puer sit patris sui heres post diem patris sui.
7 ic wylle þæt ælc cyld beo his fæder yrfnume æfter his fæder dæge.
3. Und ich will, dass jedes Kind [= Nachkommenschaft] Erbe seines Vaters sei nach seines Vaters Lebzeiten.
3. And I will that every child [= offspring] be his father's heir after his father's lifetime.
And it is my will that every child shall be his father's heir after his father's death.

note.seg: puer (s. d. Wb) heisst ‘Nachkommenschaft’, auch a. 1181 bei Madox Hist. Exchequer 297. Die Versio braucht also nicht etwa zu meinen, das Erbrecht in Land sei allein dem ältesten Sohn zugewiesen

puer (see that word in Wb) means ‘offspring’, also in 1181 in Madox Hist. Exchequer 297. The Versio therefore need not mean, say, that the right of inheritance in land is assigned to the eldest son alone

Abzulehnen ist die Deutung auf die etwa zu hindernde Absicht eines die Stadt mediatisieren wollenden Domanialherrn, Bürgereigen einzuziehen. Stubbs meinte [ich glaube: mit Unrecht], das Erbrecht sei unter Eadward III. durch Krone oder Stadt beschränkt worden. Ebensowenig darf man denken an das seit 12. Jh. nachweisbare Privileg mancher Stadt, dass Intestatgut des Bürgernachlasses von der Obrigkeit nicht ferner eingezogen werde; vielmehr s. Gl Erbgang 9d. e. 12a ff.—Ähnliches aus städtischen Freibriefen sammelt Ballard (Brit. borough chart. 74f.), der Intestates und Burgagium für gemeint hält

To be rejected is the interpretation that the aim was to forestall a possible intention on the part of a demesne lord seeking to mediatize the city to confiscate burgesses’ property. Stubbs thought [wrongly, I believe] that the right of inheritance had been restricted under Eadward III by the Crown or the city. Nor may one think of the privilege, attested from the 12th cent., of many a town that the intestate goods of a burgess’s estate should no longer be confiscated by the authorities; rather, see Gl Erbgang 9d. e. 12a ff. — Similar material from town charters is collected by Ballard (Brit. borough chart. 74f.), who takes intestacy and burgage to be meant
